name: Work Permit

requirements.blocker_text: A non-Caymanian requires a work permit to engage in gainful occupation; the application is made through a prescribed form with fees, and generally requires employer sponsorship (Immigration (Transition) Act, Section 56), except for narrow exemptions under Section 53.

Persons specified under the Act's work-permit provisions (Part 7) must comply with an approved vaccine course, evidenced by a vaccination certificate obtained no later than 14 days before the relevant application, subject to medical-certificate exemptions.

evidence_required.document: Prescribed work permit application form and fee

outcome.duration_length: not specified in the sources reviewed (the Act references maximum periods and a 'final work permit' concept under Section 66, without stating the figures in the text extracted)

sources.title: Cayman Islands Immigration (Transition) Act (2022 Revision) -- Part 7 (Work Permits): Sections 49 (specialist caregivers), 53 (exemptions), 56 (application requirements), 64 (change of employer), 66 (term limits), 67 (fees), 52A/53A (vaccination requirements)

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of the Cayman Islands' initial build, sourced directly from primary legislation. Permit-processing authority varies by circumstance among the Work Permit Board, the Business Staffing Plan Board, and the Cayman Brac and Little Cayman Immigration Board -- not modelled as separate routes since the Act treats them as parallel administrative bodies for the same underlying permit, not distinct legal categories. Section 64 allows a change of employer under 'special circumstances' (redundancy, victimisation, corporate restructuring, or written employer consent) -- flagged as a partial mitigation of the employer-tie, not modelled as its own requirement. Specific fee amounts and term-limit figures are referenced by section number in the Act's structure but were not present in the excerpted text retrieved in this pass -- flagged as a gap rather than guessed. pr_after_months (96 = 8 years) reuses the general permanent-residence threshold confirmed in ky_permanent_residence_general.json's source, on the assumption that time on a work permit counts toward that clock -- the Act's own wording ('legally and ordinarily resident') supports this but it is not explicitly restated in this section.
